title: Maple and walnut cake
subtitle: a two-layer sponge with maple in the batter and a maple buttercream between the layers
excerpt: Maple and walnut cake is a two-layer vanilla sponge where maple syrup replaces part of the sugar in the batter, giving a subtle caramel note. Toasted walnuts are folded through the sponge and scattered on the top. A maple buttercream fills and tops the two layers. The maple flavour is present but gentle; it works behind the butter and the nuts.
sourceNotes: Maple walnut cake is a classic North American recipe documented in Canadian and American cookbooks from the mid-twentieth century onward, and widely adopted in British baking since the 1990s.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the unfilled sponge layers well wrapped for up to 2 months. Fill and frost on the day of serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best assembled and served the same day. The filled cake keeps at room temperature for 1 day or in the fridge for 2 days.

content.text: Maple and walnut cake is a two-layer sponge where maple syrup replaces part of the caster sugar in the batter. The maple flavour is subtle in the sponge itself and stronger in the buttercream. Toasted walnuts give a roasted note through both layers and decorate the top.
Heat the oven to 180 degrees C (fan 160 degrees C / gas 4). Grease two 20 cm sandwich tins and line the bases with baking paper.
Beat the butter and caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Add the maple syrup and beat to combine. Beat in the eggs one at a time, then stir in the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, then fold in 80 g of the toasted walnuts, reserving 20 g for decorating the top.
Divide evenly between the two tins and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and a skewer comes out clean. Turn out onto a rack and leave to cool completely.
Beat the butter until very soft and pale, about 3 minutes. Beat in the sifted icing sugar in two additions, then beat in the maple syrup. The buttercream should be light and fluffy.

Place one sponge on a board and spread generously with half the buttercream. Place the second sponge on top and spread the remaining buttercream over the top. Scatter the reserved walnuts over the surface.

attrs.problem: Maple flavour very faint in the finished cake
attrs.avoid: Avoid light or diluted maple syrup; cheaper products have less flavour.
attrs.fix: Use 100% pure maple syrup (Grade A or B) rather than maple-flavoured syrup. Add a few extra drops of maple extract to the buttercream for a stronger result.

attrs.problem: Buttercream too runny and sliding off the sides
attrs.avoid: Avoid using warm maple syrup; it melts the butter and makes the buttercream very soft.
attrs.fix: Chill the assembled cake for 20 minutes to firm the buttercream before serving.
